description: Original fictional supers content: hero and villain codenames, power sets with limits, origins, teams, modern secret identities, lairs, headlines and incident oracles.

provenance.title: Supers synthetic corpus
provenance.creator: LexiconLang contributors
provenance.attribution: All strings in this pack are original synthetic fiction authored for LexiconLang. No real living people, trademarks or setting-specific IP are reproduced.

grammars.description: Hero codenames built from bright nouns, virtues and animal totems.
Villain codenames: sharp adjectives, cold objects and ominous titles.
A power set entry: a verb of action paired with a strange faculty.
How an ordinary person acquired an extraordinary faculty.
Hero teams, villain syndicates and semi-legitimate organizations.
Hero hideouts and villain headquarters, from rooftops to disused infrastructure.
Tabloid and broadsheet headlines about costumed incidents.
Short Public Service mottoes used by teams and vigilantes.

tables.description: A 2d6 oracle for the cost or boundary attached to an invented superhuman faculty.

result.text: Usable for only a heartbeat; the effort leaves a ringing headache.
Requires direct touch and a clear line of sight to the target.
Needs several minutes of stillness to gather a single charge.
Each use erases one cherished memory, permanently and without warning.

tables.description: A weighted oracle of strange public incidents suitable for a headline hook.

result.text: A six-block blackout resolves itself; every clock in the district runs slow.
A city bus hovers politely at an intersection until a masked figure waves it down.
Two identical figures report the same stolen umbrella at two police stations.
Every shop window on one street reflects the same impossible sunrise.
A hidden transmitter broadcasts a nine-word message in a dead language.
An unmarked cordon appears around a laundromat; nobody remembers ordering it.
A falling crane is stopped mid-air by something that leaves chalk-white handprints.
A crowd collectively forgets the name of the mayor for one entire afternoon.
A dead radio station transmits weather reports from a date three years ahead.
A hairline crack of blue light opens above the river and closes before noon.
A sealed archive releases a thousand paper cranes, each bearing a case number.
The city council unanimously votes to thank an unidentified benefactor.

tables.description: A weighted oracle of quiet warnings that precede a superhuman confrontation.

result.text: The underground rail is ten degrees colder than the platform.
A chalk circle appears overnight beneath your usual bus stop.
Your shadow arrives a half-second after you do.
Every dog on the block faces the same empty alley.
Tomorrow's paper is already on the stand, with today's date.
A streetlamp burns blue and then goes out completely.
An unfamiliar accounting ledger lists your name under 'outstanding'.
Three soft knocks come from a door that has been bricked up for years.
